name: CBD
character: Nairobi's busy central business district of offices, government buildings, shops and matatu termini. It is lively by day and much quieter after office hours.
safetyNote: Busy and generally fine by day; keep phones and bags close in crowds and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Almost every matatu route starts or ends in the CBD, with major stages around Kencom, Ambassadeur and the Railways area; commuter trains leave from Nairobi Central station.

name: Upper Hill
character: A business district of corporate towers, hospitals and government offices just west of the CBD. Mostly offices, with some apartments.
safetyNote: Calm and professional by day; it empties out in the evening, so use ride-hailing after dark.
transport: Reached from the CBD via Haile Selassie Avenue, Ngong Road and Hospital Road; matatus heading along Ngong Road pass nearby.

name: Westlands
character: A second commercial centre with offices, malls, hotels, restaurants and much of Nairobi's nightlife. Popular with visitors and young professionals.
safetyNote: Busy day and night; usual city sense applies, especially leaving bars late, so book a ride-hailing car to the door.
transport: Waiyaki Way runs through it, with many matatus to and from the CBD; the Nairobi Expressway has an exit at the Westlands end.

name: Parklands
character: An established, leafy residential area next to Westlands with a long-standing South Asian Kenyan community, apartments, schools and hospitals.
safetyNote: A settled residential area; normal precautions apply, such as not walking alone on quiet roads late at night.
transport: Limuru Road and the Parklands avenues link it to the CBD and Westlands, with matatus along Limuru Road.

name: Highridge
character: A residential area beside Parklands, made up mostly of apartments and family homes. It is often grouped together with Parklands.
safetyNote: Quiet and residential; take the usual care walking at night and use ride-hailing after dark.
transport: Served by roads connecting to Limuru Road and Parklands, with matatus towards the CBD.
verify: Check Highridge's exact location and boundaries relative to Parklands, its centre coordinates, and whether City Park counts as nearby; find a well-known landmark actually inside Highridge.

name: Kilimani
character: A densely built area of apartment blocks, cafés, restaurants and offices, popular with young professionals and expats.
safetyNote: Lively and generally relaxed; keep phones out of sight on the street and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Argwings Kodhek Road, Lenana Road and Ngong Road connect it to the CBD; matatus run along Ngong Road and Argwings Kodhek.
verify: Yaya Centre is often described as Hurlingham/Kilimani; confirm which listing it belongs in.

name: Kileleshwa
character: A leafy residential area where older houses sit alongside newer apartment blocks. Quieter than Kilimani but close to it.
safetyNote: Quiet and residential; avoid walking on unlit roads late and use ride-hailing after dark.
transport: Linked to Westlands and Kilimani via Ring Road Kileleshwa and Othaya Road; matatus are fewer than on the main corridors.

name: Lavington
character: An affluent residential suburb of large plots, townhouses and gated compounds, with a few shopping centres.
safetyNote: Calm and residential; streets can be quiet and dark at night, so travel by car after dark.
transport: James Gichuru Road links it to Waiyaki Way; there is matatu service but most residents drive or use ride-hailing.

name: Hurlingham
character: A compact mixed area of apartments, offices, clinics and shops between Kilimani and Upper Hill.
safetyNote: Busy and generally fine by day; use ride-hailing at night and keep phones out of sight on the street.
transport: Close to Ngong Road and Argwings Kodhek Road, with frequent matatus to the CBD.

name: Riverside
character: A small, upmarket area near Westlands, home to embassies, offices and apartments along Riverside Drive.
safetyNote: Calm and well kept; as anywhere, avoid walking alone on quiet stretches at night.
transport: Riverside Drive connects to Waiyaki Way and Chiromo Road; it is easiest by car or ride-hailing.

name: Spring Valley
character: A green residential suburb north of Westlands with large homes, schools and some diplomatic residences.
safetyNote: Quiet and residential; streets get dark at night, so use a car or ride-hailing.
transport: Reached via Lower Kabete Road and Peponi Road from Westlands; public transport is limited, so most people drive.
verify: Confirm that Peponi Road runs through Spring Valley and check the centre coordinates.

name: Loresho
character: A quiet, leafy residential estate west of Westlands, mainly family homes.
safetyNote: Peaceful and residential; at night, travel by car rather than walking.
transport: Accessed from Lower Kabete Road and Waiyaki Way; little matatu service inside the estate, so a car helps.
verify: Check Loresho's centre coordinates and road access (Lower Kabete Road vs Waiyaki Way), and add a well-known landmark if one exists.

name: Muthaiga
character: One of Nairobi's oldest and most exclusive residential suburbs, with large walled homes, diplomatic residences and private clubs.
safetyNote: Very quiet residential roads; there is little foot traffic, so travel by car, especially at night.
transport: Limuru Road and Thika Road run nearby; Muthaiga is mostly car-dependent.

name: Runda
character: An upmarket, mostly gated residential estate of large homes north of Karura Forest, near the UN complex in Gigiri.
safetyNote: Quiet and private; it is car-dependent, so plan rides rather than walking at night.
transport: Reached from Limuru Road and the Northern Bypass; a car or ride-hailing is the practical option.
verify: Confirm Runda's centre coordinates and which roads give main access (Limuru Road / Kiambu Road / Northern Bypass).

name: Gigiri
character: The diplomatic quarter, home to the United Nations Office at Nairobi and several embassies, with upmarket housing around it.
safetyNote: Very orderly with lots of security around the institutions; normal precautions apply, as anywhere.
transport: Limuru Road runs past it with matatus to and from the CBD; many people use ride-hailing.

name: Rosslyn
character: A leafy residential area off Limuru Road with large homes and international schools, popular with expat families.
safetyNote: Quiet and residential; roads are dark at night, so use a car.
transport: Limuru Road is the main route, with matatus to the CBD; inside the estates, a car is needed.

name: Karen
character: A spacious, green suburb in the south-west with big plots, horse paddocks, cafés and a relaxed feel. Named after Karen Blixen.
safetyNote: Calm and spread out; distances are long and roads are dark, so plan transport for the evening.
transport: Ngong Road and Langata Road link it to the city; matatus run along Ngong Road, but a car is very useful here.

name: Langata
character: A mixed residential area along Langata Road next to Nairobi National Park, with estates ranging from mid-range to upmarket and several attractions.
safetyNote: Generally relaxed; as everywhere, use ride-hailing at night and keep belongings close at busy stages.
transport: Langata Road is the main artery, with frequent matatus to the CBD.

name: South B
character: A long-established, mainly middle-income residential estate off Mombasa Road, with a strong community feel.
safetyNote: Settled and residential; normal common sense applies, such as using ride-hailing late at night.
transport: Close to Mombasa Road and the CBD, with frequent matatus.
verify: Confirm Mater Misericordiae Hospital is counted as South B.

name: South C
character: A quiet, middle-income residential estate between Mombasa Road and Langata Road, popular with families.
safetyNote: Quiet and residential; take the usual care at night and use ride-hailing.
transport: Matatus run via Mombasa Road and Langata Road to the CBD.

name: Nairobi West
character: A busy mixed area near Langata Road with apartments, student housing, small businesses and eateries.
safetyNote: Busy and generally fine by day; keep phones out of sight in crowds and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Langata Road and Mombasa Road are close by, with plenty of matatus to the CBD.

name: Madaraka
character: A compact residential estate next to Nairobi West, best known as the home of Strathmore University, with plenty of student housing.
safetyNote: Busy with students and generally relaxed; normal precautions apply at night.
transport: Close to Langata Road and Mbagathi Way, with matatus to the CBD.

name: Industrial Area
character: Nairobi's main industrial and warehousing district, full of factories, depots and wholesale businesses. Few people live here.
safetyNote: A workplace district that is busy by day and empties at night; plan a ride rather than walking after dark.
transport: Served by Mombasa Road, Jogoo Road and Enterprise Road, with many matatus at shift times.

name: Embakasi
character: A large area in the east covering many estates, from older housing to newer apartment developments, and the international airport.
safetyNote: Varies by estate and is generally fine; use ride-hailing at night and keep phones out of sight at busy stages.
transport: Mombasa Road, Outer Ring Road and the Nairobi Expressway serve it; there is also a commuter rail line to Embakasi Village.
verify: Embakasi covers a large area (several constituencies); the centre point is a rough estimate. Confirm the commuter rail station name (Embakasi Village).

name: Pipeline
character: A very densely populated estate of high-rise rental flats off Outer Ring Road, home to many young workers and families.
safetyNote: Busy and crowded; the same common sense as anywhere applies, so watch your phone in crowds and use ride-hailing late at night.
transport: Outer Ring Road and Mombasa Road have frequent matatus to the CBD and Industrial Area.
verify: Check the centre coordinates and whether the name comes from the nearby Kenya Pipeline depot; add a well-known landmark.

name: Donholm
character: A middle-income Eastlands estate near Outer Ring Road and Jogoo Road, with phased housing estates and local shopping.
safetyNote: Residential and generally fine; take the usual care at busy junctions and use ride-hailing after dark.
transport: Jogoo Road and Outer Ring Road have regular matatus to the CBD.

name: Buruburu
character: A well-known, planned middle-class estate in Eastlands built in phases, with a settled, family feel.
safetyNote: A settled residential area; normal precautions apply, especially late at night.
transport: Close to Jogoo Road and Outer Ring Road, with frequent matatus to the CBD.

name: Umoja
character: A large, busy Eastlands estate with many family homes, extensions and small businesses.
safetyNote: Busy and lived-in; keep phones out of sight at stages and use ride-hailing at night, as you would anywhere.
transport: Matatus run via Outer Ring Road and Jogoo Road to the CBD.

name: Kayole
character: A densely populated, lower-cost residential area in the far east of Nairobi, with busy markets and local businesses.
safetyNote: Busy and crowded in places; go with someone who knows the area if you are new, and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Kangundo Road and Spine Road connect to Outer Ring Road, with matatus to the CBD.
verify: Check the centre coordinates and confirm Spine Road as a main access road; add a well-known landmark.

name: Eastleigh
character: A major trading hub east of the CBD, packed with shopping malls, wholesale clothing and textiles, and excellent Somali and Ethiopian food. Home to a large Somali Kenyan community.
safetyNote: Very busy, especially at the weekend; keep phones and wallets close in crowds and dress modestly out of respect for local custom.
transport: Juja Road and General Waruinge Street link it to the CBD, with frequent matatus.

name: Pangani
character: An older neighbourhood just north-east of the CBD near the start of Thika Road, with a mix of older housing and newer flats.
safetyNote: Busy and generally fine by day; use ride-hailing at night and keep phones out of sight at stages.
transport: Close to Thika Road and Murang'a Road, with many matatus passing through.
verify: Check centre coordinates and landmarks, and whether Pangani is better grouped under 'CBD & Upper Hill' or 'Eastlands'.

name: Ngara
character: A busy older neighbourhood on the northern edge of the CBD, known for its markets, small shops and affordable student flats.
safetyNote: Crowded and busy; keep bags in front of you in markets and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Within walking distance of the CBD, with matatus along Murang'a Road and Limuru Road.

name: Kasarani
character: A growing residential area off Thika Road, known for the national sports stadium, with many newer apartment blocks.
safetyNote: Generally relaxed; there are big crowds on match and event days, so keep belongings close and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Thika Road (the Thika Superhighway) and Kasarani–Mwiki Road, with frequent matatus and buses to the CBD.

name: Roysambu (TRM area)
character: A busy stretch along Thika Road around Thika Road Mall, with apartments, shops and nightlife. It is popular with students and young workers.
safetyNote: Lively day and night; keep phones out of sight at busy stages and book ride-hailing for late journeys.
transport: Right on Thika Road at the Northern Bypass junction, with constant matatus and buses to the CBD.
verify: Confirm Garden City Mall is close enough to call 'nearby' (it is further south on Thika Road).

name: Githurai
character: A large, densely populated, budget-friendly area along Thika Road. It straddles the Nairobi–Kiambu border, with Githurai 44 on the Nairobi side and Githurai 45 on the Kiambu side.
safetyNote: Very busy, especially at the stage and market; keep phones and bags close and use ride-hailing late at night.
transport: Thika Road has frequent matatus and buses to the CBD.
verify: Straddles Nairobi (Kasarani) and Kiambu (Ruiru); listed as nairobi. Confirm that Githurai 44 is in Nairobi and Githurai 45 in Kiambu, and check the coordinates.

name: Kahawa (Kahawa West / Wendani)
character: A cluster of estates along Thika Road near Kenyatta University, full of student housing. Kahawa West is on the Nairobi side, while Kahawa Wendani and Kahawa Sukari are across the border in Kiambu.
safetyNote: Busy student area; keep phones out of sight in crowds and walk in company or use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Thika Road has frequent matatus to the CBD; Kahawa West is also reached via the Northern Bypass.
verify: Boundary: Kahawa West is believed to be in Nairobi and Wendani/Sukari in Kiambu (Ruiru) — confirm. Confirm which county Kenyatta University's main campus is in. The centre point is a compromise between the estates.

name: Zimmerman
character: A densely built residential area just off Thika Road near Roysambu, with affordable rental flats.
safetyNote: Busy residential streets; the usual city sense applies, so use ride-hailing late at night.
transport: Linked to Thika Road at Roysambu, with frequent matatus to the CBD.
verify: Check the centre coordinates and road access; add a landmark inside Zimmerman if one is well known.

name: Kibera
character: Kenya's largest informal settlement, home to a large, resilient and entrepreneurial community with many local businesses and community projects. Community-led tours exist.
safetyNote: Visit with a local community guide who can show you around respectfully, and always ask before taking photos of people.
transport: Bordered by Ngong Road and Langata Road, with matatus along both, and a commuter rail stop at Kibera.
verify: Confirm Kibera commuter rail station is currently in service.

name: Kawangware
character: A densely populated, lower-cost area west of Lavington, with lively markets and many small businesses.
safetyNote: Busy and crowded around the market; go with someone local if you are new, keep phones out of sight, and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Naivasha Road and Gitanga Road have frequent matatus to the CBD.

name: Dagoretti
character: A large area in the west of Nairobi with a mix of older settlements, rental housing and semi-rural edges towards Kikuyu.
safetyNote: Varies by neighbourhood and is generally fine by day; use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Ngong Road and Naivasha Road carry matatus to the CBD.
verify: Dagoretti is a broad area (two constituencies); check the representative centre point, and note that Dagoretti Corner is at its eastern end on Ngong Road.

name: Ngong Road corridor
character: The long main road from the CBD towards Karen and Ngong, lined with malls, offices, hospitals and apartment estates.
safetyNote: Busy and generally fine; take care crossing the road and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Ngong Road is one of the city's busiest matatu corridors, with buses to Karen and Ngong town.

name: Utawala
character: A fast-growing area on the eastern edge of Nairobi along the Eastern Bypass, with new family homes and apartments on what was recently open land.
safetyNote: Spread out and still developing; some roads are poorly lit, so arrange transport for the evening.
transport: The Eastern Bypass connects it to Mombasa Road, JKIA and Thika Road; matatus run to the CBD via Outer Ring Road and Kangundo Road.
verify: Check the coordinates and main matatu routes; add a well-known landmark.

name: Syokimau
character: A commuter suburb in Machakos County just across the Nairobi boundary off Mombasa Road, with many family homes and gated estates near JKIA.
safetyNote: Quiet and residential; distances are long and some roads are unlit, so plan rides at night.
transport: Mombasa Road and the Nairobi Expressway connect it to the city; the SGR Nairobi Terminus for Madaraka Express trains to Mombasa is in the Syokimau area, and a commuter rail line runs to Syokimau station.
verify: Confirm that Syokimau is entirely in Machakos County. Confirm the exact location and county of the SGR Nairobi Terminus (often described as at Syokimau, on the Nairobi/Machakos boundary near JKIA), and that Gateway Mall is at Syokimau.

name: Athi River / Mlolongo
character: Towns along Mombasa Road in Machakos County. Mlolongo is a busy roadside commuter town, while Athi River has an industrial and export-processing zone and growing residential estates.
safetyNote: Busy roadside towns with heavy truck traffic; take care crossing Mombasa Road and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Mombasa Road and the Nairobi Expressway, which starts at Mlolongo, link to the city; matatus run to the CBD.
verify: The two towns are about 6-8 km apart; the centre point is a compromise. Confirm Daystar's Athi River campus and the EPZ name.

name: Kitengela
character: A fast-growing town in Kajiado County along Namanga Road, south of Nairobi National Park. Many people commute from here into Nairobi.
safetyNote: Busy town centre and generally relaxed; keep belongings close at the stage and plan transport at night.
transport: Namanga Road (A104) joins Mombasa Road at Athi River; matatus run to the CBD, and traffic can be heavy at peak times.

name: Ongata Rongai
character: A large, busy commuter town in Kajiado County just beyond Langata on Magadi Road, popular with students and young families for its lower rents.
safetyNote: Busy and generally fine by day; keep phones out of sight at the stage and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Magadi Road links to Langata Road with frequent matatus, which are known for their bright decoration; an SGR station on the Naivasha line serves the area.
verify: Confirm the exact Nairobi–Kajiado boundary near Rongai, whether Multimedia University is in Nairobi or Kajiado, and the name and location of the Ongata Rongai SGR station and whether passenger trains use it.

name: Ngong town
character: A town in Kajiado County at the foot of the Ngong Hills beyond Karen, with a busy centre and quieter residential areas around it.
safetyNote: Generally relaxed; hike the Ngong Hills in a group or with a guide, and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Ngong Road via Karen has matatus and buses to the CBD; an SGR station on the Naivasha line is near Ngong.
verify: Confirm the Ngong SGR station location and passenger services.

name: Ruaka
character: A fast-growing town in Kiambu County, not Nairobi, just north of the city along Limuru Road near the Northern Bypass. It is full of new apartment blocks popular with young professionals.
safetyNote: Busy and generally fine; keep phones out of sight at the stage and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Limuru Road has frequent matatus to the CBD, and the Northern Bypass links it to Thika Road and Westlands; traffic at the Ruaka junction can be heavy.
verify: Two Rivers Mall sits at the Ruaka/Gigiri border; confirm whether it is in Kiambu or Nairobi County. Check the Ruaka town centre coordinates.

name: Ruiru
character: A large, fast-growing town in Kiambu County along Thika Road, with affordable housing, industry and the new Tatu City development nearby.
safetyNote: Busy town centre; keep belongings close at the stage and plan transport at night.
transport: Thika Road has frequent matatus and buses to the CBD, and a commuter train runs between Ruiru and Nairobi.
verify: Confirm that the Nairobi–Ruiru commuter rail service is currently running.

name: Ridgeways (Kiambu Road)
character: A residential area of homes and newer estates off Kiambu Road, north-east of Muthaiga. Ridgeways is mostly in Nairobi, but Kiambu Road beyond it crosses into Kiambu County.
safetyNote: Quiet and residential; it is car-dependent, so arrange rides at night.
transport: Kiambu Road has matatus to the CBD; most residents drive.
verify: Confirm where the Nairobi/Kiambu boundary falls on Kiambu Road (Ridgeways is believed to be mostly in Nairobi). Check the coordinates and add well-known landmarks (e.g. Ridgeways Mall or Windsor Golf Hotel, if confirmed to be here).

name: Kikuyu
character: A town in Kiambu County west of Nairobi, known for its schools and a University of Nairobi campus, and increasingly a commuter base.
safetyNote: A settled town and generally relaxed; use the usual care at busy stages and at night.
transport: Waiyaki Way and the Southern Bypass link it to Nairobi; matatus run to the CBD, and Kikuyu has a commuter rail station.
verify: Confirm that Kikuyu commuter rail services are currently running.

name: Thindigua
character: A growing residential area along Kiambu Road in Kiambu County, just beyond the Nairobi boundary, with newer apartments and townhouses.
safetyNote: Residential and generally relaxed; some roads are dark, so use ride-hailing at night.
transport: Kiambu Road has matatus to the CBD, and traffic is heavy at peak times.
verify: Confirm Thindigua is in Kiambu County, check the coordinates, and add a landmark.

name: Banana / Limuru side
character: The cooler, greener highlands north-west of Nairobi in Kiambu County. Banana Hill is a busy small town, and further on Limuru is known for its tea estates.
safetyNote: Generally relaxed and semi-rural; roads are dark at night, so plan transport ahead.
transport: Limuru Road via Ruaka and the Nairobi–Nakuru highway serve the area, with matatus to the CBD.
verify: Banana Hill and Limuru town are about 10 km apart; the centre point is a rough compromise. Confirm Brackenhurst's location and that Limuru Road reaches Banana Hill.

name: Juja
character: A university town in Kiambu County along Thika Road, home to Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT), with lots of student housing.
safetyNote: Student town and generally relaxed; walk in company at night and keep phones out of sight in crowds.
landmarks: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT)
transport: Thika Road has frequent matatus and buses to Nairobi and Thika.

name: Thika
character: A large industrial and commercial town in Kiambu County at the end of Thika Road. It is a city in its own right but connected closely with Nairobi.
safetyNote: Busy town centre; the usual city sense applies, so keep belongings close and use ride-hailing at night.
transport: The Thika Superhighway has frequent buses and matatus to Nairobi, taking about an hour outside peak times.
